correctness.rationale: The all-q,n proof identifies a necessary and sufficient seeded-hub/omitted-colour criterion; fixes a proper full colouring, counts each seeded outer clique with z^(q-2)(q-1+z), subtracts precisely q-1 synchronized omissions, and proves unique completion. Direct simulation of 357677 assignments and 224 exact algebraic profiles independently corroborate finite cases, without claiming to prove the infinite theorem.

evidence: Farr and Morgan, arXiv:2406.15746v1, define the general weighted forced-colouring domain sum.
Full inspected complete-multipartite result counts parts seeded in complete multipartite graphs with the palette equal to the number of parts.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general definition or computational reduction applies abstractly to all graphs but does not yield this closed cardinality polynomial. Windmills have several disjoint nonadjacent blades tied through one hub and are not complete multipartite when n>=2, q>=3. The chromatic-polynomial clique-separator product does not independently force the hub.

evidence: The windmill hub has degree n(q-1), versus q-1 for the previously treated one-clique graph.
For q>=3,n>=2 windmills have triangles; they are not complete multipartite, since outer vertices in different blades are nonadjacent while vertices of the same blade are adjacent.
The exact factor -(q-1)z^{n(q-2)} removes globally synchronized omitted-colour assignments when the hub is not initially coloured.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The closed new polynomial, sharp minimum and entire probability law follow from a shared-hub exclusion calculation not supplied by the one-clique or complete-multipartite formulas. A general decomposition theorem not found in searches could imply it; historical priority thus remains qualified.

originality.rationale: After statement-level comparisons with Farr 2026, Farr–Morgan 2024, paths/cycles, bipartite and multipartite forcing formulae and different ordinary zero-forcing on friendship graphs, no statement implying the uniform q,n polynomial and shared-hub obstruction was located. A possible broad older cut-vertex composition theorem is a disclosed historical-priority risk, not treated as ruled out.
residual_risks: An unindexed older theorem giving the exact forced-colouring function of clique-sums along a cut vertex could directly imply this specialization.
